The field eligibilityStatus is required in every Object Path. However, the fields:

paymentAccountReference.description:
Payment Account Reference.
The field eligibilityStatus is required in every Object Path. However, the fields:
encAccountNumber, paymentAccountReference, tokenAccountNumber,
vProvisionedTokenID, and errorResponse are conditionally required fields on one
of the Object Paths and optional in the other paths.
A Payment Account Reference (PAR) is a unique reference value associated with a
specific card holder PAN. It identifies the card account, not just a card. PAR is a non-
payment identifier that can be associated to PANs and tokens, as defined by EMVCo.
PAR allows all participants in the payments chain to have a single, non-sensitive value
assigned to a consumer.
This value can be used in place of sensitive card holder identification fields and
transmitted across the payments ecosystem to facilitate card holder identification. PAR
has a well- defined format (as per the Jan 2016 EMVCo documentation):
• Fixed length of 29 characters
• All Uppercase, Roman, & Alphanumeric values
• 4-character BIN Controller ID assigned by EMVCo followed by a 25-
character value
Important: PAR is only returned when available. PAR is not available 100% of the time.
Note PAN LCM updates are NOT processed by VIS if an Issuer opts out of PAN LCM
updates. However, PAR updates are still executed even if the Issuer has opted out of
LCM.

type.description:
Type of the installment plan as configured in Visa Developer Center/Portal by
the Issuer.
• ISSUER_PROMOTION
Applies a promotional rate as an Installment Funding Fee applicable to the
Installment Plan.
An Issuer Promotion Plan must have an explicit expiration date. These
Installment Plans are available to all Merchant Participants to display to
Eligible Cardholders
• ISSUER_DEFAULT
Applies an Installment Funding Fee typically applicable to the Consumer-
Funded Plans.
These Installment Plans are available to Sellers and Indirect Merchants to
display to Eligible Cardholders.
• MARKET
Applies a Market Rate Installment Plan.
This type of installment plan can only be configured by Visa Representatives.
These are standardized Seller Funded Installment Plans recommended by
Visa for defined tenures that Issuers may choose to provide to Eligible
Cardholders by opting into Market Plans.
The Installment Funding Fee payable as dictated by the fundedBy value for a
Market Plan may vary by country and may be revised at Visa’s discretion.
• BI_LATERAL
Applies an Installment Funding Fee different from Market Rate Installment
Funding Fee. Type of the installment plan as configured in Visa Developer
Center/Portal by the Issuer.
This Installment Funding Fee is agreed to between an Issuer and a Merchant
Participant pursuant to a written agreement between the Merchant Participant
and the Issuer.
These Installment Plans are available only to specific Merchant Participants
who have a Bilateral Plan with the Issuer pursuant to an agreement with the
Issuer.
Rules Governing Bilateral Plan Hierarchy
• If a Bilateral Plan is setup between the Issuer and the Seller, this Bilateral
Plan will take precedence over all the other Bilateral Plans.
• If a Bilateral Plan is setup between the Issuer and the indirect merchant
(who is onboarded to a Seller), then this Bilateral Plan will take precedence
as long as the Issuer does not have any Bilateral plans setup with the
Seller
• As per hierarchy, the Seller Bilateral Plan is the default plan for cardholders
unless the plan does not exist. Should there be two Bilateral Plans--one for
Seller and one for the Indirect Merchant, then the Seller Plan gets the
precedence over the Indirect Merchant’s Plan.
• In the absence of a Seller Bilateral Plan, the Indirect Merchant’s Bilateral
Plan will be selected.
• In the absence of either the Seller or the Indirect Merchant Bilateral Plans,
only then will the Issuer Default Plan, Issuer Promotion Plan, or the Market
Plan should be selected.

category.description:
Merchant Category Code (MCC)
The Merchant Category Code (MCC) is a four-digit number assigned to
describe a merchant’s primary business based on annual sales volume
measured in local currency. In addition, some MCCs identify a specific
merchant or type of transaction. Visa and its members use MCC data for a
range of purposes, including activity tracking, reporting, and risk management.
Acquirers (and their agents) are required to assign the correct MCC to each of
their merchants. Visa retains the right to require corrections to MCC
assignments and use.
The MCCs and descriptions have been derived from Standard Industrial
Classification (SIC) Codes and the International Organization for
Standardization (ISO) Codes. Please note that Visa MCCs and SIC codes do
not always correspond. In many cases, Visa has consolidated several SIC
codes into one MCC to manage the number of MCCs. In other cases, such as
for T&E and direct marketing merchants, Visa established MCCs that do not
have corresponding SIC codes.
See Visa Merchant Data Standards Manual for more info. For information
related to MCC codes, please navigate to this link about Supplier Locator.

type is required in both Object Paths. Besides type, one of ratePercentage, or
flatFee are the required fields.
• CONSUMER – Fee for Consumer-funded plan
• CONSUMER_UPFRONT – Upfront fee that Consumer must pay to Issuer
• MERCHANT_FUNDING – Fee for Merchant-funded plan must pay to Issuer
• MERCHANT_SERVICE – Service fee charged to the Merchant by Visa

ratePercentage.description:
Interest fee rate in percentage applied on Installment payment.
• Percentage rate is a non-negative value.
• The percentage value is represented with two implicit decimals. (max
10000) Example: 250 specifies 2.5%
• For calculations, the actual percentage value should be interpreted as
follows: actualPercentageValue = ratePercentage / 100.00
type is required in both Object Paths. Besides type, one of ratePercentage, or
flatFee are the required fields.
Should flatFee be provided, then ratePercentage is not required and becomes
an optional field.

monthlyRatePercentage.description:
Monthly interest fee rate in percentage applied on Installment payment.
This will only be set for fee type, “CONSUMER”.
• Percentage rate is a non-negative value.
• The percentage value is represented with two implicit decimals. (max
10000) Example: 250 specifies 2.5%
• For calculations, the actual percentage value should be interpreted as
follows: actualPercentageValue = ratePercentage / 100.00

flatFee.description:
Flat fee applied on the first Installment payment in Issuer currency.
• The amount is only represented in minor units. For example, in cents for
USD currency.
• There are no fractional minor units; they are rounded to a whole number
in minor units.
• The currency field contains the number of minor units (per ISO 4217).
For example, “123112” in USD represents the amount, USD 1231.12.
type is required in both Object Paths. Besides type, one of ratePercentage, or
flatFee are the required fields.
Should ratePercentage be provided, then flatFee is not required and becomes
an optional field.

MatchedEligibleInstallmentPlansAPIFeeInf.description:
Fee rate table used to calculate the Seller fees.
• The feeInfo will contain an array of fee type(s) with the associated
ratePercentage or flatFee.
• One or many of the fee types—CONSUMER, CONSUMER_UPFRONT,
MERCHANT_FUNDING, and MERCHANT_SERVICE might be present based
on the plan type and plan setup.
• MERCHANT_FUNDING and MERCHANT_SERVICE appear only when the
API request is initiated by Acquirers.

installmentFee.description:
The consumer fee for this installment period. This fee corresponds to
the feeType – CONSUMER.
All Amount fields use a representation in minor units only. For example, in cents
for USD currency.
There are no fractional minor units; they are rounded to a whole number in minor
units.
The currency field contains the number of minor units (per ISO 4217). For
example, “123112” in USD represents the amount, USD 1231.12.

totalAmountExcludingUpfrontFee.description:
The total amount payable for this Installment period, including the
principal amount and consumer fee, but excluding any upfront fee. The currency is
specified in the parent object that includes this structure.

amount.description:
All Amount fields use a representation in minor units only. For
example, in cents for USD currency.
The principal amount for this Installment period. The currency is specified in the
parent object that includes this structure.
There are no fractional minor units; they are rounded to a whole number in minor
units.
The currency field contains the number of minor units (per ISO 4217). For
example, “123112” in USD represents the amount, USD 1231.12.

upfrontFee.description:
The consumer upfront fee for this Installment plan and is included only
on the first installment.
• This fee corresponds to the fee type, CONSUMER_UPFRONT
• Conditionality - This is available only on the first Installment.
It is a numerical value in the minor units of the currency, such as Cents for USD. If
the currency is USD, “13400” is used for representing the amount, "$134.00".
Note that there are no fractional minor units represented. They're rounded to the
whole minor units.

totalAmount.description:
The total amount payable for this installment period, including principal
amount, consumer fee, and any upfront fee. The currency is specified in the parent
object that includes this structure. The amount is represented in minor units. It is a
numerical value in the minor units of the currency, such as Cents for USD.
The currency field contains the number of minor units (per ISO 4217). For example,
“123112” in USD represents the amount, USD 1231.12. There are no fractional minor
units; they are rounded to a whole number in minor units.

encAccountNumber.description:
Encrypted Personal Account Number (PAN or Card Number)
The fields vPlanID, orderInfo/transactionInfo, and acceptedTAndCVersion
are required fields in every Object Path. However, encAccountNumber,
vProvisionedTokenID, paymentAccountReference, tokenAccountNumber, or
tokenReferenceID are conditionally required fields on one of the Object Paths and
optional in the other paths.
JWE - This is a URL-safe base64-encoded string that represents the encrypted payload for
AccountNumber. The format is the JSON Web Encryption using asymmetric/symmetric key
material made available at time of onboarding. It is a standard JWT with a single custom
AccountNumber claim, “accountNumber” that contains the card number/PAN.
Visa uses JSON Web Encryption (JWE) to encrypt sensitive information in APIs. For more
info, see Encryption (JWE) Details.
Important: For Non-Visa cards, the encAccountNumber field is the most appropriate
option to pass PAN/token.

vProvisionedTokenID.description:
Provisioned Token ID of the Card/PAN. This is the token information
corresponding to the PAN tokenized by the TokenRequester. The token requester is
usually the Seller.
The fields vPlanID, orderInfo/transactionInfo, and acceptedTAndCVersion
are required fields in every Object Path. However, encAccountNumber,
vProvisionedTokenID, paymentAccountReference, tokenAccountNumber, or
tokenReferenceID are conditionally required fields on one of the Object Paths and optional
in the other paths.
Token Conversion to PAN
In the past, when Issuers enrolled an entire Account Range of cards, Merchants were not
able to use tokens for them. As of the 23.09 release, Visa tokens can be used for cards
enrolled using Account Ranges. If vProvisionedTokenID is provided, it will be converted
to PAN.

acceptedTAndCVersion.description:

auto-incremented every time an update is made to the Plan by the Issuer in the Visa
Developer Center/Portal UI. This is the same as Plan.termsAndConditions[i]version
sent to the Seller in the response of the matched plans API.
Note: The Terms and Conditions text field may contain encoded HTML entities
(such as, ampersands). The field text must be decoded to remove any HTML
entities before being presented to the consumer.
The fields vPlanID, orderInfo/transactionInfo, and acceptedTAndCVersion
are required fields in every Object Path. However, encAccountNumber,
vProvisionedTokenID, paymentAccountReference, tokenAccountNumber, or
tokenReferenceID are conditionally required fields on one of the Object Paths and
optional in the other paths.

paymentAccountReference.description:
Payment Account Reference.
A Payment Account Reference (PAR) is a unique reference value associated with a specific
card holder PAN. It identifies the card account, not just a card. PAR is a non-payment
identifier that can be associated to PANs and tokens, as defined by EMVCo. PAR allows all
participants in the payments chain to have a single, non-sensitive value assigned to a
consumer. This value can be used in place of sensitive card holder identification fields and
transmitted across the payments ecosystem to facilitate card holder identification.
PAR has a well-defined format (as per the Jan 2016 EMVCo documentation):
The fields vPlanID, orderInfo/transactionInfo, and acceptedTAndCVersion
are required fields in every Object Path. However, encAccountNumber,
vProvisionedTokenID, paymentAccountReference, tokenAccountNumber, or
tokenReferenceID are conditionally required fields on one of the Object Paths and optional
in the other paths.
• Fixed length of 29 characters
• All Uppercase, Roman, & Alphanumeric values
• 4-character BIN Controller ID assigned by EMVCo followed by a 25- character
value
Important: PAR is only returned when available. PAR is not available 100% of the time.
Also, PAR is not supported for Non-Visa cards.
Note PAN LCM updates are NOT processed by VIS if an Issuer opts out of PAN LCM
updates. However, PAR updates are still executed even if the Issuer has opted out of LCM.

tokenAccountNumber.description:
EMVCo Token Account Number.
The fields vPlanID, orderInfo/transactionInfo, and acceptedTAndCVersion
are required fields in every Object Path. However, encAccountNumber,
vProvisionedTokenID, tokenAccountNumber, or tokenReferenceID are
conditionally required fields on one of the Object Paths and optional in the other paths.
Token Conversion to PAN
In the past, when Issuers enrolled an entire Account Range of cards, Merchants were not
able to use tokens for them. As of the 23.09 release, Visa tokens can be used for cards
enrolled using Account Ranges. If tokenAccountNumber is provided, it will be converted
to PAN.
Important: For Non-Visa cards, tokens must not be passed in the tokenAccountNumber
field as this is not supported.

Note that there are no fractional minor units represented. They're rounded to the

provided, it is used to enforce the maximum amount applicable for this Plan Acceptance.

acceptanceChannel.description:
Default: "IN_PERSON"
Specifies the channel through which the transaction is initiated, and payment
information is collected.
• When specified in Eligibility requests this value indicates the
merchant preferred channel for the transaction.
• When specified in Plan Acceptance requests, this value indicates
the channel through which the transaction was made.
• Though optional, we highly recommended that you provide this
value. Should this value not be provided, Acceptance Channel
would be considered as IN_PERSON option.
• "IN_PERSON" - Indicates transactions initiated via In-Store/Face-
to-Face.
• "E_COMMERCE" - Indicates transactions initiated via e-commerce
websites.
Note: This field is technically optional to maintain backwards
compatibility. But it can be regarded as Conditionally Mandated for the
following reason: This information is used as a filter and
if E_COMMERCE is not specified, the value will default to IN_PERSON.
When the value defaults to IN_PERSON, some merchants may not get
installment offers with certain Issuers who are only enrolled for
E_COMMERCE transaction and not IN_PERSON.

PlanSelectionAPIPreferences.description:
Object (Preferences)
Allows Seller Enablers to specify the Capabilities or Preferences of Merchants on whose
behalf this request is made.
This is an optional parameter which must be provided when required. Please carefully go
through the specific fields in this object to understand how this impacts your implementation.

visIndicatorCapability.description:
Specifies the Merchant Acquirer’s VIS flag handling capability.
• "SUPPORTED" – Indicates that the Merchant Acquirer supports the
Seller’s Plan Registration System Identifier and will include the
identifier in its ISO Auth and Clearing messages.
• "NOT_SUPPORTED" - Indicates that the Merchant Acquirer does
not support the Seller’s Plan Registration System Identifier and will
not include the identifier in its ISO Auth and Clearing messages.

PlanSelectionAPICapabilities.description:
Object (Capabilities of the Merchant when enabler acts on behalf of the
Merchant)
Capabilities of the Merchant handled in this request. Valid in context of the
Enabler acting on behalf of the Merchant.

category.description:
Merchant Category Code (MCC). Either category or
partnerMerchantReferenceID is required.
Should partnerMerchantReferenceID be provided, then category is not
required and becomes an optional field.
• The Merchant Category Code (MCC) is a four-digit number assigned
to describe a Merchant’s primary business based on annual sales
volume measured in local currency. In addition, some MCCs identify a
specific Merchant or type of transaction. Visa and its members use
MCC data for a range of purposes, including activity tracking, reporting,
and risk management. Acquirers (and their agents) are required to
assign the correct MCC to each of their Merchants. Visa retains the
right to require corrections to MCC assignments and use.
• The MCCs and descriptions have been derived from Standard
Industrial Classification (SIC) Codes and the International Organization
for Standardization (ISO) Codes. Please note that Visa MCCs and SIC
codes do not always correspond. In many cases, Visa has consolidated
several SIC codes into one MCC to manage the number of MCCs. In
other cases, such as for T&E and direct marketing Merchants, Visa
established MCCs that do not have corresponding SIC codes.
See Visa Merchant Data Standards Manual for more info.
For information related to MCC codes, please navigate to this link about Supplier
Locator.

PlanSelectionAPIMerchantInfo.description:
Seller-specific information used for filtering/searching or authorization or
reporting.
The fields vPlanID, orderInfo/transactionInfo, and acceptedTAndCVersion
are required fields in every Object Path. However, encAccountNumber,
vProvisionedTokenID, paymentAccountReference, tokenAccountNumber, or
tokenReferenceID are conditionally required fields on one of the Object Paths and
optional in the other paths.
The fields merchantInfo and preferences are optional fields on all the Object Paths.

vTransactionID.description:
ISO Visa Authorization Transaction ID. A unique value that Visa
assigns to each transaction and returns to the Acquirer in the authorization response.
Visa uses this value to maintain an audit trail throughout the life cycle of the
transaction and all related transactions, such as reversals, adjustments,
confirmations, and chargebacks.
In case of Post Purchase scenario, if Visa Transaction ID differs between
authorization and clearing, this value should refer to clearing Visa Transaction ID.
Note
In transactions using Mastercard credentials, where a single transaction ID is not
available, Participants should use the Mastercard Tran ID field. Tran ID is made
up of Financial Network Code + Banknet Reference Number +
MMDD(TransactionDate)concatenated with no spaces.
Either vTransactionID, or one of authCode, currency,
transactionAmount, or dateTime are the required fields.
Should one of the other fields mentioned be provided, then vTransactionID is not
required and becomes an optional field.
Important
In the Post Purchase scenario, Plan Selection is only supported for Transactions that
occurred within the past 31 days.

externalTransactionRef.description:
ISO transaction auth code (alphanumeric). This is used by external clients
as an opaque identifier and is sometimes used to correlate multiple transactions.
externalTransactionRef and installmentTransactions are optional in
every Object Path.

authCode.description:
ISO transaction auth code (alphanumeric). This Field 38 in ISO 8583
contains the response identification assigned by the authorizing institution.
For Post Purchase scenario, this field may not be populated if it’s not sent in Plan
Selection API.
Either vTransactionID, or one of authCode, currency,
transactionAmount, or dateTime are the required fields.
Should one of the other fields mentioned be provided, then authCode is not required
and becomes an optional field.

transactionAmount.description:
Transaction amount.
Either vTransactionID, or one of authCode, currency,
transactionAmount, or dateTime are the required fields.
Should one of the other fields mentioned be provided, then transactionAmount is
not required and becomes an optional field.
All Amount fields use a representation in minor units only. For example, in cents for
USD currency.
There are no fractional minor units; they are rounded to a whole number in minor
units. The currency field contains the number of minor units (per ISO 4217). For
example, “123112” in USD represents the amount, USD 1231.12.
• In case of During Purchase scenario, this value must always be provided.
• In case of Post Purchase scenario, this value need not be provided and will
internally be set as the sum of clearing amounts
(installmentTransactions.clearingAmount)
When returned in the response body or callback notifications:
• This field is populated if provided by the merchant/seller in the request and
represents the transaction amount of the Visa ISO transaction authorization.
• When returned to the Issuer in a multi-currency scenario, this field will be
populated in the Issuer’s currency. Before all clearings are received, the
indicative foreign exchange rate (during Plan Acceptance) will be used for
conversion. After all clearings are received, the clearing foreign exchange
rate will be used for conversion.

currency.description:
Currency of the transaction amount. Currency Code in ISO 4217 format.
Either vTransactionID, or one of authCode, currency,
transactionAmount, or dateTime are the required fields.
Conditional Mandatory Field :
• Always required when transactionAmount is specified
• Should one of the other fields mentioned be provided, then currency is
not required and becomes an optional field.

dateTime.description:
Original transaction date and time sent by Seller. This also helps with the
accuracy of the lookup of the transaction when vTransactionID is not provided.
Either vTransactionID, or one of authCode, currency,
transactionAmount, or dateTime are the required fields.
Should one of the other fields mentioned be provided, then dateTime is not required
and becomes an optional field.
Important
In the Post Purchase scenario, Plan Selection is only supported for
Transactions that occurred within the past 31 days.

PlanSelectionAPITransactionInfo.description:
This structure represents the fields required for identifying a Visa transaction.
The fields vPlanID, orderInfo/transactionInfo, and acceptedTAndCVersion
are required fields in every Object Path. However, encAccountNumber,
vProvisionedTokenID, paymentAccountReference, tokenAccountNumber, or

Important:
This field is required only when there is no orderInfo provided in this API

clearingAmount.description:
Clearing amount for the transaction in settlementCurrency.
This field is used when the plan acceptance is associated with a clearing, most
used in a post-purchase use case. This field will always be populated by Visa
Installments when clearing data is available.
An Amount structure. minLength: 1 maxLength: 999999999999999

settlementCurrency.description:
Currency of the clearing/settlement amount. Required when
clearingAmount is present. The code is in ISO 4217 format.

clearingDateTime.description:
Clearing date and time as set by the card network. This is the
information in the clearing data sent to the issuers by the card network. This
field will be always populated by Visa Installments when clearing data is
available.
• When returned in the HTTP response body or callback
notifications, the time value will default to '00:00:00Z' when only
the clearing date is available from the source system.
• When used in the HTTP request body of an API request to Visa
Installments, the value must conform to the date-time format.

acquirerReferenceNumber.description:
Acquirer Reference Number (ARN) is a 23-digit identification
number associated with every draft and voucher. It consists of a Format Code,
BASE Identification Number (BIN), Capture Date, Film Locator, and Check
Digit. The ARN should be unique although duplicate ARNs will not be rejected.

PlanSelectionAPITransactionInfo2.description:
This structure represents the fields required for identifying a Visa
transaction.

vInstallmentTransactionID.description:
Installment Plan schedule ID. Visa-generated identifier for a clearing
associated with this plan acceptance. This is useful if there is more than one clearing
associated with a plan acceptance as ISO Transaction is not sufficient to identify a plan
acceptance, as there can be more than one plan acceptances associated with a single
ISO transaction.
Either vInstallmentTransactionID or status or one of clearingAmount,
settlementCurrency, or clearingDateTime are the conditionally required
fields.
Should one of the other fields mentioned be provided, then
vInstallmentTransactionID is not required and becomes an optional field.
There can be more than one vInstallmentTransactionID per plan acceptance in
the case of multiple clearings and partial ISO transaction associated with a plan
acceptance.

status.description:
Status of the ISO Transaction's Clearing associated with a plan
acceptance.
Either vInstallmentTransactionID, or status, or one of
clearingAmount, settlementCurrency, or clearingDateTime are the
required fields.
Should one of the other fields mentioned be provided, then status is not required
and becomes an optional field.
• CONFIRMED - Clearing received and InstallmentTransaction is
confirmed
• CANCELLED - Cancel request received and canceled
• PENDING_CONFIRMATION – Authorization received and waiting for
clearing match in Visa Installments
• PENDING_CANCELLATION - Cancel request received and waiting for
original clearing
• PARTIALLY_REFUNDED - Cancel request received and transaction amount
partially refunded

clearingAmount, settlementCurrency, or clearingDateTime are the
required fields.
Should one of the other fields mentioned be provided, then clearingAmount is not
required and becomes an optional field.

Should one of the other fields mentioned be provided, then settlementCurrency
is not required and becomes an optional field.

category.description:
Merchant Category Code (MCC). Either category or
merchantReferenceID is required.
Important: This field is Conditional, which means it’s required on the condition that there
is no merchantReferenceID provided in this API. Should merchantReferenceID be
provided, then category is not required and becomes an optional field.
The Merchant Category Code (MCC) is a four-digit number assigned to describe a
Merchant’s primary business based on annual sales volume measured in local currency.
In addition, some MCCs identify a specific Merchant or type of transaction. Visa and its
members use MCC data for a range of purposes, including activity tracking, reporting,
and risk management. Acquirers (and their agents) are required to assign the correct
MCC to each of their Merchants. Visa retains the right to require corrections to MCC
assignments and use.
The MCCs and descriptions have been derived from Standard Industrial Classification
(SIC) Codes and the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) Codes. Please
note that Visa MCCs and SIC codes do not always correspond. In many cases, Visa has
consolidated several SIC codes into one MCC to manage the number of MCCs. In other
cases, such as for T&E and direct marketing Merchants, Visa established MCCs that do
not have corresponding SIC codes.
See Visa Merchant Data Standards Manual for more info.
For information related to MCC codes, please navigate to this link about Supplier Locator.

partnerMerchantReferenceID.description:
Reference used by Partner to identify Merchant or Merchant Chain.
Conditional Mandatory Field: This field is always required when the API call is made by the
(Merchant) partner on behalf of the Merchant.
Usually, this reference ID is assigned by the Partner but in cases where not provided
when onboarding the Merchant, this value will be generated by Visa and provided to the
Partner. It is used by Visa for enforcing authorization (so that one Merchant's plan
acceptance is not accessed/modified by an unauthorized merchant/partner), risk
assessment and for instrumentation. It is also used to serve bilateral plan agreements
between a Seller and Issuer. In the future, it can be used to specify merchant-specific
filters for installment plans.
• When provided in cancellation or search, this ID is used to match the plan
acceptances and enforce authorization
• When provided in plan selection (plan acceptance creation) API, it is saved to be
used later for search plan acceptances.
• When provided in plan match API, it is used for instrumentation/ reporting purposes.

paymentAccountReference.description:
Payment Account Reference.
A Payment Account Reference (PAR) is a unique reference value
associated with a specific card holder PAN. It identifies the card account, not
just a card. PAR is a non-payment identifier that can be associated to PANs
and tokens, as defined by EMVCo. PAR allows all participants in the
payments chain to have a single, non-sensitive value assigned to a
consumer. This value can be used in place of sensitive card holder
identification fields and transmitted across the payments ecosystem to
facilitate card holder identification.
PAR has a well- defined format (as per the Jan 2016 EMVCo
documentation):
• Fixed length of 29 characters
• All Uppercase, Roman, & Alphanumeric values
• 4-character BIN Controller ID assigned by EMVCo followed by a 25-
character value
Important: PAR is only returned when available. PAR is not available 100%
of the time. Also, PAR is not supported for Non-Visa cards.

available.

time value will default to '00:00:00Z' when only the clearing date is
available from the source system.

Installments, the value must conform to the date-time format.

clearingAmount, settlementCurrency, or clearingDateTime are
the required fields.

fully CANCELLED state.

refundAmount, and lastRefundDateTime are always optional fields
under every Object Path.

the nearest whole number in minor units.

under every Object Path.
